source.title: The Computational Value of Sensory-Aligned Receptive Fields Depends on Neuronal Expressivity
source.authors: Agnese Adorante; Aaron Spieler; Anna Levina

record.tranche_reason: Tests the value of sensory-aligned, restricted input connectivity using a recurrent ELM model and budget-matched random-input controls, rather than comparing conventional convolutional and fully connected networks.
record.gate_note: The paper compares aligned structured input with random input, tests scrambled and task-irrelevant coordinates, and compares full input and ℓ1 regularization. Prior-work comparisons in the Related Work section are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study tests sensory-coordinate restrictions in recurrent Expressive Leaky Memory networks, not convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers. Its structured-versus-random comparisons and auditory full-input baseline do not measure V3's architecture comparison. None of V1–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' interpretation: task-aligned receptive fields improve ELM generalization, their advantage decreases at high neuronal expressivity, and generic sparsity induces selectivity but only partly recovers structured-input benefits. Qualify the evidence: the memory dependence is not monotonic on DVS-Gesture, all SHD memory-sweep contrasts are nonsignificant, and the remaining regularized-versus-structured accuracy deficit is nonsignificant (−1.19 points, q=0.092), although the train–test gap remains significantly larger.
record.recipe_differences: Uses recurrent ELM networks with fixed synapse budgets and sensory-coordinate input wiring, rather than the conventional convolutional versus fully connected comparisons described in V3. Optimizer: Adamax; datasets: SHD, DVS-Gesture, CIFAR10-DVS.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with task alignment (motion versus spatial coordinate), coordinate scrambling, network size, neuronal memory capacity, and full-input versus structured wiring.

fits_no_version.finding: Task-aligned ELM input restrictions significantly improve accuracy in several conditions; task-irrelevant and scrambled-coordinate contrasts are nonsignificant. Some network-size contrasts are also nonsignificant.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sensory-coordinate-aligned input restrictions can improve recurrent ELM classification over budget-matched random wiring, depending on task alignment and network size.

fits_no_version.finding: SHD structured-input advantages are nonsignificant throughout the memory sweep. DVS-Gesture advantages remain significant, increase through M=13, and fall to +2.47 points at M=21.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The value of sensory-aligned wiring depends on ELM memory capacity, with a reduced advantage at the highest tested capacity but no general monotonic decrease.

fits_no_version.finding: On SHD, full-input ELM networks have lower test accuracy and larger train–test gaps than frequency-restricted networks. Additional ℓ1 regularization improves accuracy and narrows the gap; its remaining accuracy difference from structured input is nonsignificant, while its gap remains significantly larger.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Frequency-restricted ELM inputs can generalize better than full inputs on auditory classification, and additional feed-forward sparsity regularization partially recovers these benefits.

record.problems: The study uses one network family and a small set of tasks and sensory geometries, as the authors note. Each condition uses 10 seeds. CIFAR10-DVS absolute accuracy is relatively low and the setup is not optimized for absolute performance. Several plotted accuracy and memory-sweep values are not numerically reported in the text or tables.
record.rows_left_out: No reported comparison from Appendix C is separately extracted: the paper states that recurrent structure produced no consistent improvement relative to uniform recurrence, but this tests recurrent topology rather than the feed-forward receptive-field/locality comparison in V3.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width beyond the zero-training-error threshold in converged one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, locality's contribution to that difference, learned sparse local connections, and initialization from a trained convolutional network.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization and dependence on tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error; dropout is present but is not varied.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, not claims that the ELM comparisons are unreadable. Table 4 provides exact values and q-values for every memory-sweep row. The study discusses V3's motivating literature but does not test that architecture-specific claim. Missing is empty because no omitted result tests V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on random labels or compare natural-label and random-label generalization.
Does not test one-hidden-layer ReLU networks or width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Does not compare conventional convolutional networks against fully connected networks, test learned sparse connections, or initialize a fully connected network from a trained convolutional network.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or tune optimizer recipes.
Does not vary batch size or test large-batch training.
Does not test dropout or its interaction with data augmentation.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare generalization measures.
Does not remove memorized examples or retrain after example removal.

relation.reason: The introduction and related work discuss convolutional locality and architectural priors, while the study's own experiments address a different architecture comparison.

tranche.reason: The experiments compare sensory-coordinate wiring within recurrent ELM networks. They do not compare convolutional and fully connected image classifiers or test another listed version.

source_check.notes: All SHD memory-sweep contrasts are nonsignificant; the DVS-Gesture advantage decreases only at the highest tested capacity, not monotonically. The remaining regularized-versus-structured accuracy deficit is nonsignificant; repeated contrasts are not independent evidence.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Task-aligned structured input on SHD at N = 110 and 210, DVS-Gesture at N = 64 and 128, and spatially structured input on CIFAR10-DVS
reader_labels.reason: Structured input has significantly higher test accuracy than the budget-matched random control in these conditions (R2, R3, R6, R7, R19).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SHD at N = 60 and 310, DVS-Gesture at N = 32, and the tested memory-capacity sweeps
reader_labels.reason: Some structured-versus-random differences are not significant; increasing neuronal memory reduces the advantage, with convergence on SHD and a residual gap on DVS-Gesture (R1, R4, R5, R8, R9, R10, R11, R12, R13, R14, R15).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Full-input networks and ℓ1-regularized full-input network on SHD
